Sorry for the wall but I want to make sure I explain things correctly.

I work seasonally at Gamestop and would like to apologize about your situation. I'm not a manager or anything big/significant like that, so don't take this as me trying to save face for the company (I get paid minimum wage and have shit hours, I'm not overly in love with GS). But as a gamer who has been very excited about getting limited edition items and unable to rapidly secure a preorder I can relate to your disappointment. It sucks but it will (probably) get better. (I say probably because there is no way to guarantee a new inventory shipment)

In an attempt to cheer you up, here's something you could do to secure a copy as well as a look from an inside perspective on what is going on. (please hear me out)

Why this happened…

In short, every store is judged by it's size and location when the inventory count is being distributed for a recently announced game or system. The smaller the store, the less inventory it will get. The bigger the store the more inventory it will get. Every store in the Gamestop chain is pulling from the same pile, and big items usually sell out on the first day. If your local store is sold out, check online. If it's also sold out online then it's sold out in the entire country.

That being said, just because it's sold out doesn't mean Gamestop won't be getting more allocations. In fact, if something does sell out that gives them an incentive to get more shipments since it means that item will probably sell well (Nintendo items are the main exception to this). The first couple waves of inventory allocations are usually smaller than ones that come later so don't give up. You're sure to get what you want eventually.

That being said...

I can't promise that your store didn't single you out or ignore your request intentionally. What I mean is that it is entirely within their power to ignore your request or just put you at the bottom of the list if you've done something to warrant that type of reaction. I can't speak for all stores, but for the most part it's really hard to get on a stores blacklist (I'm talking sexual harassment, stalking, theft… stuff like that). But that probably didn't happen.

How to secure a copy…

Checking up every day to see if they've gotten a new allocation. I'm not saying bother them to the point where it's annoying (meaning two or three times a day), but don't be afraid to call once a day or check online. If you're a regular to your store then they will want you to get your item. Happy customers are return customers, and if you know each other well enough they will want you to get your game because they know how important it is to you. I speak from experience.

This same thing happened to me when Microsoft and Sony announced the X1 and PS4. I was unable to secure a "Day One Edition" of the Xbox One at first since my local store was super small and only got a small amount of items in the first wave (this was before I was working there). I was already on a first name basis with the employees there so I didn't feel weird calling/visiting every day and asking if they had gotten a new shipment yet. They put my name on a list the way they did for you, and about three weeks later they got a new allocation and I was guaranteed a console.

TL;DR - Don't worry if Gamestop says they're sold out of something. They will get more items before long and probably want you to get your game (they're gamers too so they've probably been there). Just make sure your name is on a list, don't bug them about it to much but don't let them forget either, and try to remain positive/optimistic. If you're in a good mood they'll want to help you more than if you get mad about things they can't control. :)
